Comments: On February 19, 2019, the Department conducted an investigation on the Chief Oil & Gas LLC Raimo Pad. A split hose caused a spill of base oil outside of containment off the well pad. The operator estimates about 1 bbl of base oil had spilled. At the time of inspection, the soil of the impacted area has been excavated. The soil has been placed in covered roll-off containers. The excavated area did not appear to have any visually impacted soil remaining. The Department spoke with Jeremy Watson with Chief Oil & Gas LLC. He said that Waste Management was coming to do a profile of the contaminated soil and haul it away. During the investigation, the operator was cleaning and removing timber mats. There was a vac truck onsite to remove the wash water out of the spill containment. The Department spoke with Peg Farrell on the phone. The Department discussed that the Act 2 process should be started. The release of base oil of the well pad is a violation of CSL 402(b), 78a 56(a), and SWMA 301.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2021
Comments: On July 27, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Harmon Creek Well A 11323 Well Site in Smith Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported by the Operator to the Department on 7/26/2021 at 16:00. The Operator reported that approximately 1.5 barrels of production water and condensate was released to the well pad due to a sight glass o-ring failure on the Gas Production Unit (GPU). At the time of inspection, the Operator was in the process of the removing the GPUs from the area impacted by the release. I observed a petroleum odor and dark staining under the middle GPU and excavated channels on either side of the middle GPU. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 30’ x 10’ in size. The staining was visible approximately 12" in depth. I spoke with Range Resources representative Nick Reda. Mr. Reda indicated that the released material was proximity 51% production water and 49% condensate oil and that the Range intends to utilize Act 2 for cleanup. No waterways were impacted by the release and no apparent migration of the material was observed. Two roll off waste disposal boxes were on site to collect the impacted material for disposal. The Operator is in compliance with the current Department spill policy for reporting the release. Violations area being issued for the release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 973525
Permit API: 015-23687
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Leroy Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/26/2022
Comments: Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake, Environmental) called the DEP yesterday afternoon to report a metal waste oil tote fell off a forklift and ruptured. It leaked an estimated 30 gallons of oil onto the pad surface. I spoke with Aaron Stredny (Chesapeake) on site who showed me where the spill occurred on the north end of the pad. The oil spilled on top of a water puddle and floated on the water. A vac truck removed the oil immediately after the spill. Then a skid steer scraped ~1" of the pad surface in approximately 100'x100' area and placed ~11 tons of pad material on liner containment. They finished the cleanup about 1 hour after the spill.Creston Environmental is screening the spill area today with a MiniRae 3000 photoionization detector (PID) and collecting confirmatory soil samples. I used a MiniRae 3000 with a 10.6 eV bulb to screen test holes in the excavated area. The highest reading was 0.7 ppm, indicating a negligible presence of volatiles in the pad material. I spoke with Aaron Vaughn (Chesapeake, HSE). He explained the oil spill was gear oil drained from equipment on site.I spoke with Marty Balada (Chesapeake, Company Man). He explained the 4 Marcellus wells here are already hydraulically fractured. Cudd's coil tubing unit started drilling out the plugs yesterday; they expect to finish drilling plugs in about 8 days.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water of 3 separate puddles on the pad surface have electrical conductivity of 0.40-0.55 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35.Violations cited to the 015-23687 well permit are considered immediately corrected. Air temp 59FJLP

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 872395
Permit API: 059-24428
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-23
Comments: On 12/19/19 a malfunction with the GPU occurred, causing the vessel to explode. On 12/20/19 OGI Joel Keller conducted inspection 2974755 and noted soil staining and a damp appearance. OGI Keller requested a follow up inspection be conducted by a WQS. On 12/23/19 at approximately 0800 I conducted a follow up inspection. The temperature was well below freezing at the time of inspection. Upon arriving at the explosion location I observed water on the access road that was not frozen, despite the freezing temperature. A soil conductivity probe was utilized and a reading od 12.02mS was observed (see photograph). Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed throughout the access road and on the east side of the access road. Trees and shrubs on the east side of the access road appeared wet. The liquid was not frozen and appeared to be brine, as further demonstrated by elevated soil conductivity readings in the area. No other trees or shrubs appeared wet, except for those east of the GPU location where elevated soil conductivity was observed. Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed further North toward the well head on the east side of the access road (see photographs). Elevated soil conductivity readings were also observed adjacent to brine tank 2. The highest reading observed was 12.83mS. Both brine tanks were severely corroded and brine tank 2 exhibited a large hole (see photographs). Brine tank 1 exhibited several smaller holes that appeared to have occurred due to shrapnel from the GPU explosion. The gravel in the former GPU location appeared to be stained, but the soil conductivity was not elevated. The Department recommends the visually impacted material is removed. Soil sample 3402-076 was collected from an area exhibiting elevated soil conductivity. Soil sample 3402-077 was collected from an area on the northwest portion of the site in an area that appeared to be unimpaired with low notably lower soil conductivity (see photographs). The Department recommends the spill is addressed consistent with the Act 2 process.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 9/05/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 9/05/2025
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8248041
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-19 to Range Resources Appalachia Llc in Frazer Twp, Allegheny county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Range Resources Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-19
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 878699
Permit API: 003-22572
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-02-19
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to an inspection (2987454) conducted in response to a complaint that was received by the Department on 2/21/2020. Assisting in this inspection is WQS Trainee Andrew Zadzilko and WQS Supervisor Samantha Foulk. Operator representative Brandon Carson is on site as well. Mr. Carson advised that drilling operations had ceased and most of the temporary storage tanks had been removed from the site. The Act 9 Sign is on site and appears to be in good condition. A strip of exposed soil directly in front of the Act 9 Sign is observed. Mr. Carson advised that this probably occurred in association with the removal of a temporary water line. The Department recommends that this exposed soil be stabilized and protected against accelerated erosion as soon as possible. The large temporary storage tank associated with the Schiller to Bakerstown Rd water line that was on site appears to have been removed. It appears that fresh stone has been put down on the access road. It appears that sediment may have left the access road and washed into the tree line (Photo 3 & 5) adjacent to the temporary storage tank pad. The Operator has placed CFS and straw at this location. The Department recommends that the operator monitor this location during rain events to ensure that the CFS is adequate to filter stormwater runoff at this location. There are long strips of exposed soil along the access road of various widths down to where the temporary water line once crossed the access road. The Department recommends that the operator stabilize these areas as soon as possible to prevent accelerated erosion from occurring. At several spots along the access road at outlet pipes there is CFS put up (Photo 7-10). The Department requests that the operator monitor these locations for any excessive sediment conveyance and to ensure that CFS is holding up during stormwater events. The Department also requests BMP inspection logs from 1/27/2020 2/19/2020. The well pad and adjacent tank pad appear to have an excessive amount of mud on them (Photo 6 & 11). According to the plan set, the gravel pad detention basin should be maintained with at least 4 inches of 2A on top of 12 inches of R3. Based on this observation violations will be issued for failure to maintain this BMP. Several locations around these pads also have exposed soil (Photo 12 & 13). One (12) is on the berm behind the well pad associated with the temporary water line the other (13) is next to the outlet structure to the infiltration basin. The Department recommends that these areas be stabilized against accelerated erosion as soon as possible. Based on this inspection violations are being issued for failure to maintain the well and tank pad against accelerated erosion. Further violations may be issued based on operator responses.

Report Details

Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/04/2025
Comments: On 03/04/2025 representatives from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently completed wells onsite and their American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers are posted at the site entrance; I was unable to confirm if the wells were tagged due to them currently being covered (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which did not contain any standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure did not contain any standing water. The tanks were labeled as per the Department's request (photos #5 and 6). A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and held in secondary containment (photo #7).Numerous upright brine tanks and temporary storage tanks are still noted onsite and held in their respective secondary containment structures which appear to be functioning as intended (photos #8 and 9). Multiple lined and covered residual waste containers are in use onsite for ongoing Act 2 remediation efforts as well as disassembly of the pad wide containment system (rig matting) and tear down of completions equipment (photos #10 and 11). The modular aboveground storage structures (MASS) have been removed and the brine offload area has been disassembled (photo #12).Remediation remains ongoing from the releases on 12/04/2024 and 12/09/2024 (Inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285) as the areas formerly covered by rig matting and containment structures are now accessible. Pad drainage systems remain shut in to prevent any water from ice and snow melt from leaving the pad. I did not observe any diesel sheen on the pad surface. Water is being removed from the well pad via an onsite vacuum truck as it accumulates. The area located underneath the brine offload area from the release on 12/09/2024 is currently being excavated to comply with Act 2 remediation standards (photo #13). Soil in this area field measured for electrical conductivity at ~1.68mS/cm and fluids accumulating in this area field measured for EC at ~15.67mS/cm (photos #14 and 15). These soils and fluids are being collected via vacuum truck or lined residual waste container.Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed at the time of this inspection due to snow coverage. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review in the mailbox at the site entrance (photo #16). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #17). The basin inlet remains shut in and no fluids or diesel sheen was observed (photo #18). Soil in the basin field measured for EC at ~0.72mS/cm (photo #19).Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Inspection Date: 2020-05-21
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (6) wells on the CAPPUCCI pad. The CAPPUCCI 2H, N2H, 4H, N4H, 102H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a new gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/18/20 @ ~ 08:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The CAPPUCCI 2H is a 2 string well, with (20¿x 9 5/8¿) and (9 5/8¿x 5 ½¿) annuli. - The HJMM WYO 1H and CAPPUCCI N4H wells (20¿x 13 3/8¿) annulus have an open casing top in cellar. Comments: On 04/17/2025 the DEP conducted a routine inspection (IR #3960352) of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) Them Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) 1.8-3.45 mS/cm. The DEP collected samples. On 05/07/2025 the DEP received the sample results and cited violations (IR #3974712). On 10/08/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) THEM Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and partly sunny. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0915 hours.The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There were two infiltration berms onsite. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) between 190.7-904 us/cm. There were four produced fluid tanks equipped with an internal secondary containment. There were six gas processing units (GPUs) onsite. There were ten temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. There were six wells capable of producing. They were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers.This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.The following violations remain open against API #015-23911:35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)I departed at 1015 hours.

Violation ID: 949212
Permit API: 015-23529
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2022
Comments: Chesapeake Appalachia (CHK) called in a release of produced fluid at 14:48 on 3/24/22. The release was found around 13:30 the same day. It was reported that at least 1 barrel of produced fluid was released from secondary containment. I arrived onsite on 3/25/22 and met with Aaron Stredny, CHK, and Creston. The fluid was released from and improperly sealed hatch on the temporary storage tank onsite. The fluid then leaked from secondary containment through a hole in the corner. A lease operator was onsite earlier in the morning and did not notice any issues. It is believed that the release occurred during the morning of 3/24/22 until its discovery around 13:30. When I arrived an area behind the tank was already excavated to a depth of 6-12 inches. I checked conductivity of puddles and soil with Creston. The soil and puddles to west were below 1000 microsiemens. Moving east from the excavated area toward the pad berm puddles and soil were elevated upto 7800 microsiemens in some areas. Additional soil and puddles were checked outside the pad along the fill slope and into the neighboring field. Results were below 500 microsiemens. The excavation will continue in the areas of elevated conductivity to the west and under the secondary containment. CHK is waiting for Mountain Energy to remove the temporary tank and containment in order to excavate the area. Before the tank is moved surrounding puddles will be removed. At least 3 tri-axle loads were excavated. It is requested that CHK perform remediation of the site according to the requirements of Act 2 and provide the requested information indicated in this inspection.

Comments: On June 22 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Prigg Morgan 11272 Well Site due to an incident. Accompaying in today's inspection was Derek Zofchak (Range Resource Representative), Nick Reda (Range Resource Representative) and Tyler Metzger (ET DEP)The findings were as follows:This inspection is in response to several E and S BMP failures on the Prigg Morgan Well Site. In a phone call from Range Resource Representative Dennis Furmacek, they reported that they had 3 separate sections of temporary E and S BMP silt sox were overtopped and or displaced. This resulted in sediment to leave the LOD and settle into adjacent vegetative field. The failures were identified during a post precipitation inspection conducted on 6/16/2023. Mr. Furmacek also indicated that waters of the commonwealth were not threatened and sediment was not discharged into the waters of the commonwealth. During today's inspection, the Act 9 Sign was on site but not permanently installed. The access road appeared to be stable with no observed erosion or sedimentation concerns. The ESCGP drawings, PPC plan and ER plan were on site. Also on site was the site inspection records for 6/16/2023 recording the E and S BMP silt sox overtopping and 6/19/2023 which recorded the remediation efforts at the well site. The CFS that was effected in the three different locations were all re-staked. Each area that was affected outside of the LOD were mulched and reseeded.Based on today's inspection, The Department will conduct a subsequent inspection to continue to evaluate remediation efforts.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8153363
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Violation ID: 8264942
Permit API: 125-28534
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: East Finley Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/19/2026
Comments: On 2/19/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the MOR 44 Pad Well Site following receipt of an incident report from the operator. The incident report was received on 2/18/2026; operator reported incident on 2/15/2026 (CTS #395229). Also on site was CNX representatives Bruce Carpenter and Chad Eisenman.Per operator report on 2/15/2026 at 06:46 am:On 2/15/2026 at 05:30 am, a pinhole was discovered in a water dump line and was misting production fluid onto the ground at an approximate quantity of 5-40 gallons; release is secured and contained; waterway not affected; cleanup crew SPSI onsite.Prior to this inspection, I spoke with Bruce Carpenter via phone call on 2/18/2026 who confirmed the received information of the spill and informed me the impacted area was remediated.During this inspection, CNX representatives indicated the spill was immediately addressed, and promptly remediated by SPSI; affected waste material was properly disposed of into roll-off containers that were no longer onsite. Based on their findings, spill was approximated to be 20 gallons.The following was observed:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance, including mailboxes and container; site plans, Emergency Response Plan, Preparedness Prevention and Contingency Plan, and all related documentation was available (Photos 1,2).-Site entrance and access road (Photos 3,4).-The impacted area and material appeared remediated from the location in accordance with 78a.66. Total approx. remediated area of reported spill 8 L x 10 W; section of pipe replaced (Photos 5-7).-Conductivity probing of immediate and surrounding areas did not indicate any impacted/contaminated material (Photos 813).Violations to be issued: 78a54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301
